title: quantization-bandwidth-shift-and-interconnect-pressure-probe
content:
TL;DR:
We observed that aggressive int8-like quantization (4/8-bit group-wise) reduces GPU DRAM pressure but can increase inter-GPU interconnect utilization in some tensor-parallel sharding layouts. That shift creates new tail-latency modes under peaky traffic because compute becomes memory-bound on a per-GPU basis while collectives see higher effective bandwidth demand. This doc captures the test matrix, measurement harness, key findings, and quick mitigation ideas.

Background / motivation:
- Going to lower-precision kernels is expected to reduce bandwidth to weights and activations on-device and therefore reduce end-to-end per-token cost.
- But quantization changes the micro-pattern of loads/stores (smaller element reads, different alignment) and sometimes increases frequency of small DMA transactions or forces different kernel tiling that increases cross-GPU communication density.
- We need to understand when quantization helps overall latency and when it inadvertently shifts load into the interconnect (NVLink/PCIE) and NCCL collectives, causing tail cases.

Hypothesis:
1) Per-layer group quantization increases non-contiguous reads and may increase PCIe host-staging for small weight chunks on some backends.
2) Reduced compute time (faster matmuls) compresses communication windows: collectives see higher instantaneous bandwidth leading to queuing/backpressure on links and NICs.
3) Tensor-parallel partitioning choices (row vs column sharding) change whether the extra collectives are point-to-point heavy or broadcast-style; that affects NVLink bisection stress.

Test matrix (short):
- Models: 7B dense (LlamaX-style), 13B transformer (longer layers), and a 70B-like sliced model for synthetic stress.
- Precision variants: fp16 baseline, hybrid-gptq-int8, dynamic-4bit (group=128), per-tensor fake-8 (for control).
- Shards / parallelism: TP-only (2x, 4x), TP+PP (2x TP + 2 stage PP), replicated no-TP (control).
- Transport configs: GDR enabled/disabled, host-staging forced, NCCL_P2P=1/0, NCCL_ALGO=ring/tree (where supported).
- Traffic shapes: steady (5k qps emulated), peaky (spikes to 40k qps over 10s), single-shot (cold start long context).

Hardware used:
- DGX-station-like rack: nodes with A100 40GB x8, NVLink fully connected per-node, Mellanox CX6 IB for cross-node.
- Single-node and two-node tests.

Measurement harness / tools:
- Request driver: go-based synthetic driver that can emit arrival patterns (steady / poisson / burst) and collect per-request token latency at 1ms resolution.
- GPU traces: nsight-systems (nsys) capture for selected runs, plus CUPTI-derived counters for memory transactions.
- NCCL tracing: built-in NCCL logging with CC_WRAPPER and NCCL_DEBUG=info to capture collective timing and algorithm selection.
- Perf/OS: sar, ethtool counters, IB stats, and dmesg for driver-level warnings.
- Kernel-level sampling: nvlink_util / nvkernels snapshot per-step (scripts in repo).

Scripts / commands (notes to self):
- start harness: ./bin/synthdriver --model 7b --precision gptq --tp 4 --qps 5000 --shape poisson --run-id QBS-20260202-01
- nsys capture: nsys profile -o /tmp/qb-run1 -t cuda,nvtx,nccl ./serving_binary ...
- collect NCCL: export NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1; NCCL_DEBUG=INFO; NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=ALL

Key observations (summary):
1) Aggregate token latency decreased for most precisions (int8-like) in single-node steady runs by ~12-25% compared to fp16. BUT tail latency (95/99) increased in bursts for TP=4 configurations.
2) nsys slices show compute kernels finish earlier with quantized kernels, but the NCCL allreduce/allgather windows compressed: the same bytes had to be transferred in a shorter wall-clock time, increasing instantaneous link utilisation by 1.8–2.3x.
3) On two-node tests with NVLink bisection and IB cross-node, we saw queue buildup on host-staging pathways when GDR was disabled. Small read sizes (sub-4KB) created many DMA transactions causing increased PCIe interrupts and host CPU consumption.
4) For TP row-shard vs column-shard: column-shard patterns tended to create many small point-to-point exchanges (worse latency in bursts) while row-shard concentrated into fewer larger collectives (better amortization).
5) NCCL algorithm selection mattered: ring vs tree tradeoffs changed sensitivity to compressed windows—tree-style had lower tail on bursts at the cost of slightly higher median.

Representative numbers (single-node A100 x8, 7B model, TP=4):
- fp16 median token time: 18.6 ms, p95 34.2 ms, p99 58.7 ms
- gptq-int8 median: 14.8 ms (-20%), p95 38.9 ms (+13%), p99 75.2 ms (+28%) during peaky traffic
- instantaneous NVLink util (sampled): fp16 peaks ~55 GB/s, gptq peaks ~110 GB/s (same total bytes but compressed time window)

Anomalies / interesting traces:
- Run QBS-20260202-17: during warm-up phase a single GPU reported a driver-level retry on a PCIe transaction; system logged increased host interrupt rates and a tombstoned NCCL rank momentarily, causing a 200ms outlier. Likely host staging handshake timing coupled with small DMA bursts.
- In some runs enabling GDR reduced CPU interrupt storms and removed the huge outliers — suggests bypassing host fixes small packet amplification.

Interpretation / root causes (working hypotheses):
- Kernel tiling + group-quant decoding increases frequency of small unaligned loads, which on some drivers result in more PCIe transactions (read amplification).
- Faster compute compresses collective windows. NCCL and HW interconnects are dimensioned for some smoothing — when many ranks try to push bursts at once they hit link buffers and start head-of-line blocking, increasing tail.
- Cross-node IB path is more sensitive because host NIC queues + kernel drivers introduce additional backpressure when bursts align.

Immediate mitigations to try (short list):
- Add micro-sleep / pacing between micro-collectives (in runtime) to spread traffic across a slightly longer window. Tradeoff: increased median but reduced tail.
- Force larger chunk sizes for weight fetches (group-quant decode to produce cache-aligned chunking) to reduce DMA amplification.
- Prefer row-shard layouts for quantized TP when acceptable.
- Ensure GDR enabled on supported infra; fall back to host staging with coalescing if not.
- Tune NCCL_ALGO and NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME to prefer topologies that reduce bisection stress (tree where bursts are common).

Longer-term engineering items:
- Add a microbenchmark in the runtime that measures "collective pressure" per model precision and suggests a default pacing factor automatically at model load time.
- Work with model-ops to provide quantization profiles including preferred chunk alignment metadata.
- Investigate more aggressive kernel fusion that reduces intermediate DRAM touch and therefore reduces interconnect need.

Open questions / TODOs (priority ordered):
- [P0] Re-run two-node IB cross-test with GDR on/off at multiple qps shapes to quantify cross-node penalty precisely (Diego to run, target 2026-03-05).
- [P0] Add instrumentation to runtime to measure per-collective instantaneous bytes/sec and expose it to Console (Ethan + Priya).
- [P1] Try staggered batching (micro-delay) prototype in the runtime to test tail improvement vs median cost.
- [P2] Talk to driver team about small-DMA amplification and ask for DMA coalescing knobs; file ticket (JIRA-1103).

Notes to self / rough action items:
- stash traces on s3: s3://redwood-perf/quant-bw-shift/ -- include nsys .qdrep and raw log bundles.
- follow-up PR to add "quant-chunk-size" config when loading gptq (PR draft exists linked_above).
- validate that our streaming path doesn't re-introduce small-packet echo when using streaming + kv-cache replay.

References and links:
- github PR (profiling harness): https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/874
- JIRA-1037: quant-bw-shift investigation epic
- internal confluence: confluence://perf/quant-bw-shift

Status: draft — want to iterate after Diego's IB runs.

-- Priya
